newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda won't comment on Ford platform - sharing.
newsitem.headline: Mazda won't comment on Ford platform - sharing.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said on Wednesday it had no comment on a local media report that it will use standardised platforms in its and Ford Motor Co's mainstay cars and recreational vehicle (RV) models.

Jiji news agency reported on Wednesday that Mazda and Ford would share standardised platforms for their new compact RVs in 1999, Mazda's MPV minivan and Ford's new RV around the year 2000, Mazda's Capella and Ford's Mondeo in 2001 and Mazda's Familia and Ford's Escort in the year 2002.
A car platform comprises a chassis and suspension. Mazda is owned 33.4 percent by Ford.
"We cannot comment about specific model names. We have not yet disclosed any details on platform issues and we are still studying whether to disclose our decision or not," a Mazda spokesman said.

Mazda said in January it was considering sharing car platforms with Ford and planned to make a decision by the end of March. Issues under consideration included which models should share standardised platforms and whether the move should include standardisation of engines and transmissions.
